(2024). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (IN.AI Research; University of Waterloo; The Ohio State University; Carnegie Mellon University; University of Victoria; Princeton University)
description: MMMU is a massive multi-discipline multimodal benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level problems requiring expert-level perception, subject knowledge, and reasoning. It contains 11.5K carefully selected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 image types.
name: MMMU
rai:annotatorDemographics: The dataset was manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects. The paper also states they recruited over 50 university students specializing in the selected majors as annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Data quality control involved lexical overlap and source URL similarity to identify potential duplicate problems, followed by author review to eliminate duplicates. Problems were also distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, and authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels; approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, quizzes, and other study materials, and created new questions based on their expertise where necessary. They were instructed to follow copyright and license regulations, avoid sites prohibiting copying or redistribution, select questions without immediately available answers to reduce contamination, ensure each question contains one or more images, is written in English, meets college-level difficulty, is unambiguous, and annotate fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation if present.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly notes that the manual curation process may carry biases. It also states that annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to address data contamination concerns in foundation models.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was collected in three stages: the authors first selected subjects from common university majors where visual inputs are commonly used; then they recruited over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in those majors to collect multimodal questions from textbooks, online resources, quizzes, and lecture materials and create new questions when necessary; finally, the collected set underwent cleaning, format checking, typo checking, and difficulty filtering.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data consists of multimodal questions drawn from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, free online resources, and other study materials, including interleaved text and images such as diagrams, tables, charts, photographs, music sheets, chemical structures, maps, medical images, and other image types.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After collection, the data underwent duplicate removal using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, format and typo correction by co-authors, and difficulty categorization into very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of questions categorized as very easy were excluded from the benchmark. The final dataset was split into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing and curation included identifying suspected duplicate problems via lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review to eliminate duplicates, format standardization, typo correction, categorization by difficulty, exclusion of approximately 10% of very easy problems, and storing each sample in structured JSON with standard naming conventions and file-path interleaving for images.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The appendix includes a version change log documenting changes from V1 to V4, with updates on Dec. 18, Dec. 21, and June 13, including corrected homepage URL, updated model names, added results, and other revisions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames MMMU as important for monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled adult labor in many industries, leading to risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The authors also argue the benchmark can help stimulate development of next-generation multimodal foundation models while cautioning that it is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to evaluate multimodal models on expert-level perception, subject knowledge, and reasoning across college-level tasks; to benchmark large multimodal models; to monitor progress toward Expert AGI; and to stimulate development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes college-level questions from domains such as Health & Medicine and Public Health that may contain medical content in questions and images. The annotation protocol explicitly instructs annotators to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
